notes.title: NEW YORK MAP EXPLAINED – DEVBLOG 2
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Greetings, aspiring journalists and media moguls![/b][/h3]
  
[h3]As we’re approaching our Closed Beta, we’d like to share more info about one of the key game mechanics.[/h3]

As an influential publisher navigating the bustling streets of 1930s NYC, you will unlock different areas of the city based on reader interest.   
[i][b]Picture it:[/b][/i] you'll be expanding your readership one neighborhood at a time, aiming to claim the coveted title of New York's most influential publisher!    

Now, let's talk about the map layout of the game, a design decision that posed quite the challenge...  

[b]Originally, our vision was to connect all districts[/b], mirroring real-life urbanization. A simple street-crossing would usher you into a different area—simple, right?  

However, reality hit, presenting us with [b]unique challenges[/b]:  
[list]
[*]How do we strategically position factions and quest givers early on, ensuring a continuous stream of challenges for you?  
[*]How do we create a smooth progression system that seamlessly unlocks areas in sync with your evolving skills and mastery level?[/list]
Enters the [b]reworked[/b] version:  
[list]
[*]We've created paths to expedite the unlocking of shops and encountering of quest givers.  
[*]Challenges now align more closely with your skill level at any moment!  
[*]You, as a player, will have greater control over your progression and can focus on elements that better fit with your playstyle. [/list]
[h3]Now, let's take a deep dive into the inner workings of the map in News Tower.  [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h1]NEW-YORK MAP[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/e9ac747f046c35f2457b9cd34e8e4e3ceb7a9d95.png[/img]

[b]The map is made up of 48 DISTRICTS waiting to be unlocked.[/b]

Each week, you get to decide which district to unlock. 
To do so, you just need to align your content with the readers interest.  
Upgrading your production line is key to meeting their increasingly difficult interest.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/54e75a46ad9b60813fe52e844405869b51a1c749.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3][b]CHOOSE WHICH SHOPS TO UNLOCK FIRST TO BOOST YOUR PRODUCTION[/b][/h3]

Once you’ve reached certain locations, you can unlock specific items with your hardly earned [i]influence points[/i]. 
The shops are tied to specific ‘Tags’ (Society, Economics, Sports, Entertainment, Crime and Politics) depending on their location – you will unlock the entertainment boost item at the Ritz Theatre of course!  
Unlocking these boosts is a game-changer, as it will help to enhance your reporters' skills and, in turn, your production line. 
[b]So, choose your path wisely for early unlocks! [/b]

[i]Some shops will also unlock new technologies and upgrades for your newspaper. 
Getting security items to stop Mobsters coming, advertising production and copy-editing to make better articles will also be unlockable at some shops. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/3e41a358b7a67466aeaf5914eeff34bcb19862f8.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3][b]REACH THE FACTIONS[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/25df2447abc7a0ed08e319d5a28be10b5a282d5d.png[/img]

We wanted to give you the opportunity to encounter factions quite early in your journey, adding an extra weekly quest to your plate. 
Progressing with the different factions will give you both money and influence points- if you succeed in their weekly quest! 

So if you are [i][b]REALLY[/b][/i] good, you can unlock one district and one quest line per week but… It’s not an easy task and you’ll need to have a good combination of tags in the same week. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3]Stay tuned as we will work on improving how factions are vying for influence in New-York City during Early Access! [/h3]

notes.title: REPORTING THE NEWS - DEVBLOG 1
notes.notes:
Greetings, aspiring journalists and media moguls, 
 
As we’re approaching our Closed Beta, we’d like to share more info about one of the key game mechanics.   
As an influential publisher in 1930s NYC, you’ll need to send your reporters to [b]find the hottest news[/b]. 
That’s why we wanted to tell you about our design decisions regarding [i]News Reporting[/i]. 
  
[h1][b] 
REPORTING MENU [/b][/h1]
  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/ae8b6ade22ed8e6ef17f0502ce220561fd5e968e.png[/img]

 To give you the best experience of being a publisher we wanted to focus on:  
[olist]
[*] Simple storytelling  
[*] Enough choices in how and what news you want to cover  
[*] Understandable in a glimpse as it’s a core gameplay element 
[*] A system that can easily be expanded upon for a richer experience later on.   
[/olist]
  
[h2][b]Managing the size of the news: [/b][/h2]

Some news will contain multiple stories to cover. Every additional story you decide to cover will change how big the news will be, but it will also take longer to get.  
For example this news have 2 stories to cover, so you can send two reporters at the same time !

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/fbabdb1711bed9c0a7443810b1ce9d64e47a21c2.png[/img]

[b]As time is your primary resource in News Tower you might rush the news despite missing key elements[/b], and sales, to get it ready for the Sunday press.  

[h2][b] 
Managing which type of news, you want to cover:  [/b][/h2]

[b]Every week you can challenge yourself[/b] to get specific types of news, should it be to unlock new areas of New York city depending on reader interests or fulfill a quest for one of the influential characters you will meet.  
Every news article contains at least one Story Tag. Some are basic, others will need extra work from your reporters, which means a longer time where your reporter is away.  
Story tags can be the following:  
[list]
[*] Politics 
[*] Tragic
[*] Educational
[*] Lies
[*] Exclusive
[*] Scandal
[/list]
 
To do so we implemented, not so long ago, the [i]“News researcher”[/i] which allows you to select which types of news you want to focus on.  

We believe this [b]lets you be in charge[/b] of what you want to print and which type of newspaper you want to run, instead of leaving you in the hands of fate.  

Your reporters will come with 3 topics they can cover out of the 6 we have in the game. 
You’ll need to choose wisely which reporter you will send as they won’t be available for some time.  
Don’t run out of reporters if you don’t want to miss out on key stories.  

For example below : 
 Earl Brown can cover[i] crime, sports and society[/i] while Peter Grey can cover [i]economics, entertainement and politics.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/da42bec77937e85f2f18bd4d0a417f9a51e920f4.png[/img]

[h2][b]Upgrading the speed of news reporting:  [/b][/h2]
There are various elements that can affect your news reporting:  
Travel options  
Improved reporter skill levels
Buff their working place
Unexpected events
 
Using those will either take time for your reporter to get experienced or cost you hard earned money, and honestly who really needs to travel by train, when a bus for 12h is comfortable enough. 
  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/28eccbaa07f215fa9a8cbe1ab6583be0f3227360.png[/img]

notes.title: Interview with the Devs - Meet the Team!
notes.notes:
[h3]Making our debut in the Future Games Show![/h3]

News Tower is participating in the [b]Future Games Show 2023[/b].

The Future Games Show is one of the industry’s flagship gaming showcases and is rapidly building a reputation as one of the best ways to discover new games!
We are very thrilled and proud to feature our game there among other exciting titles!

We felt this was the perfect time for us to give you an update on how the game has been evolving, what we have been working on and developing since 2021!

[h3][b]MEET, in this interview:[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Jan-Maarten - Creative Director
[*]Maxime - Game Designer
[*]Iris - Illustrator & Graphic Designer
[*]Louis - Brand Manager[/list]
Stay tuned to meet the rest of the team in a later episode!! :D

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3][b]What inspired you to create a game set in this specific time period?[/b][/h3]
 
[i][b]Jan-Maarten[/b][/i]
-
In 2018 I came upon an article about the New York Times newspaper production in 1941. It had a series of pictures showing every department from Newsroom to Printroom. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/944e30a3bbc2711745ccf0bd7d7cf6710dd87547.jpg[/img]

Filled with awesome analog machines and oozing with a sense of nostalgic craft. 
Coming from an art school background I always had an affinity for letterpressing and movable type. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f398a18e553d40959f9d8a38884f8b6720141feb.jpg[/img]

I have always been a big history enthusiast and when a Newspaper Tycoon first came to mind, the 1930s seemed like a perfect fit. It’s a really interesting decade because it was in constant uproar by a global economic and political crisis that ultimately led to the second world war.
Prohibition, Famous Mobsters, Hollywood Golden Years, the rise of Jazz, the Great Depression, the Dust Bowl... It felt that for a tycoon game, where stories are the main resource, this decade would never be short of providing Interesting material.
And New York City just felt like a natural central point to base the News Tower in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]
 
[h3][b]What's the most challenging aspect of developing a tycoon?[/b][/h3]
 
[i][b]Jan-Maarten[/b][/i]
-
A Tycoon game consists of hundreds of little systems coming together. This means that it took a really long time to create somewhat of a working prototype. That made it really hard to judge if we were working on something great or not. For lots of game devs it's always tricky to know if you are making the right choices but for a tycoon game, for a long time you're just in the dark. Having a core idea that everybody is enthusiastic and feels good about really helps to keep things going. Nowadays it's just really hard to change any system when it's connected and depending on so many other elements. Just accept that half of the time the project doesn’t run and you're in for lots of rewrites. It's a marathon but a fulfilling one at it.

[i][b]Maxime[/b][/i]
-
The most complicated design aspect of a tycoon is the risk of accumulating too many mechanics to give life to an autonomous and coherent "ecosystem". This genre-specific systemic density can turn into an overflow of information, phases or resources. Because of this density, the balancing work is much more demanding than in any other game genre.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3][b]Tell us about a unique or innovative gameplay mechanic that you've included in the game![/b][/h3]
 
[i][b]Jan-Maarten[/b][/i]
-
It's always tricky to say what's innovative about your own project. But we do feel that we're 
adding new interesting elements to an established Tycoon landscape.
News Tower has very rounded play phases: Report, Process and Print. Which makes it ideal for shorter 15/30 min play sessions to more casually go through the game if that fits your playstyle. Where the Process Phase is the more known tycoon element of building and managing and there is lots of that. Report and Print bring new unique mechanics to the genre.

[h3]Reporting[/h3]
Choosing what stories to report on and assigning the right reporters alters the news item resource composition. Do you go for Hot-topics and gain lots of new readers or abide by some influential outside party's hidden agenda. We want the player to feel like their choices matter and really put them in the publisher seat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/927042b495f9062428fff1b9c7833375827092c4.gif[/img]
 
[h3]Newspaper Print Composition[/h3]
Players can arrange their Newspaper to their own liking. This visual element really brings the newspaper to life and shows the choices a player made earlier. For instance, when you've sent a photographer to the news location, that article will show a photo. The headlines also reflect the story paths you chose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/66e94fccbd5c138e122c3d77f29417108f15c9b1.gif[/img]

[b]FREE PRO TIPS HERE ⬇[/b]
Make sure you leave room for one of those juicy ads. Because staying profitable is one of those golden Tycoon rules that everybody understands.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]

[h3][b]What are the key elements you considered when creating a compelling Key Art for News Tower?[/b][/h3]
 
[i][b]Iris[/b][/i]
-
The Key Art needs to reflect the game ambiance and to be attractive at the same time. 
Here, the New York's 1930s period and the journalism theme are the main focus. 
The architecture, with the skyline, the roof water reservoir, the iconic Empire State Building or the characters wearing old-fashioned clothes and using old technologies, are all elements who are here to give you a narrative context and suggest the gameplay thematics.

[b]⬇ Here you can see a before/after of the Key Art, highlighting the many changes ⬇[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f54c3252c589831767dd4df3f94f11691283360c.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]
 
[h3][b]Can you walk me through the step-by-step process of creating a Key Art for News Tower?[/b][/h3]

[i][b]Iris[/b][/i]
-
First, the development team gave me a brief with some suggestions about the graphic content and the atmosphere. With their notes, I've made some quick sketches trying different compositions, character types and logo placement.
Then, we started to identify what is important to keep, which size the elements should be to deliver a clear message. They selected one drawing and from there I made a new version using the game graphic style and color palette.
I draw everything in Illustrator. We started to move elements again, as colors changed all the image balance. A key art needs to be understandable no matter the size, even in a really small format. To achieve this, we simplified some elements. For exemple, initially, the tower was open, showing the environment in which most of the game happens. We realizes that closing it allows you to focus more on the environment as a whole, not being frustrated by the little details you struggle to see.  
When we were sastisfied, the final step started. The entire game visuals are made with vectors. To create something that fits the game and at the same time brings an element of surprise and newness, I've used vectorial art as a background for a digital painting with warmer organic lights and textures you won't find in game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40684736/f17fb7887a81a54a9206921d60ff3d0e614a3f55.png[/img]
 
[h3][b]What role does the Key Art play in the marketing strategy?[/b][/h3]
 
[i][b]Iris[/b][/i]
-
It's a really important part, the creator's vision of the game needs to be highlighted in the key art. In a way, it's a quick static trailer, giving you the desire to see and know more about the game.

[i][b]Louis[/b][/i]
-
We have been working for a while on the new visual identity of News Tower. With the production progressing every day, it was time to update the key art of the game.
The key art is an essential visual for a game - especially for indies! When a game appears on the home page or in your searches, this is the first visual you’ll see. It must show major elements of the game and be recognizable for players!
 
We felt that some elements were missing for the player to dive properly into our game atmosphere and universe. The tower was already there, but how would a business run without a team? As the 30s news are the game core, it was important for us to accentuate the immersive side of the key art and to add the setting of your future (old) newspaper business: New York! 
A touch of the Empire State Building, a bit of old-fashioned clothes and a lot of journalism... and you get this new key art! 
I spare you technical marketing terms and the looonnnnggg description of the process to find the perfect result… but don’t worry our graphic designer came out unscathed!

notes.title: Happy New Year From News Tower HQ!
notes.notes:
News Tower HQ wishes all of you a happy new year!

2022 will be an exciting year for us. Since the October Edition of Next Fest 2021, we have been working hard on new features, bug fixes and AI improvement to deliver the Early Access version of ‘News Tower’ to Steam this year. (New) features which we have been working on include:

- Totally revamped the way you report on news offering more depth and gameplay.
- You can now choose a direction of your newspaper and work your way towards targets which apply to this direction to satisfy and reach your readers.
- No more hard requirements on news. You can only do better.
- News items now have categories and a quality mark which play an important role in reaching your audience targets.
- A different and more simple mechanic for ads.
- News can now have ‘risks’ attached to it like lawsuits or injury points for your employees which adds more depth to the choices you make.
- Added an overview screen of all your employees
- Employees now have traits giving them unique characteristics which can be useful in many aspects of the game.
- Added category bonuses: you earn more points by placing similar categories on the same page of your newspaper.
- Enhanced hints for placing buff objects. Preview areas where placing accessories makes sense.
- Skill/Leveling system for employees actually works now.
- Search the globe more efficiently using filters for category or news quality.
- A working kitchen with a cook.
- Shared waiting lines for toilets and coffee machines.
- Employees take elevators based on congestion, not randomly.

Also improved the general AI, have been working on further game performance optimizations and (obviously) lots of little bug fixes.

We’re very excited for what’s to come this year and about all improvements and features. We hope you are as well and are looking forward to sharing the EA release of News Tower with all of you.

Stay tuned.

News Tower HQ
